items.article: "You Can See Everything" is a shocking and funny look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes' life. Here's what I can share without spoiling it. My row of Alice Tully Hall was filled with reporters scribbling notes about the buzzy new Elizabeth Holmes documentary . Then, we heard the warning. "In the interest of trying to preserve a relatively spoiler-free experience for later audiences, we ask that you not film and post this conversation," said Dennis Lim, the artistic director of New York Film Festival. Lim recommended shaming anyone who recorded the chat between Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the directors of "You Can See Everything." A flock of journalists put their phones away, disappointedly. The filmmakers had reason to worry: "You Can See Everything" was one of the most shocking, revelatory, and oddly funny films I've ever seen. It was twisty and worthy of seeing with fresh eyes. So, I'm not going to spoil it for you. Lim wouldn't want me to. Here's my veiled, semi-secretive attempt to tell you what I saw. The line wrapped around the block. items.article: On Hawaii Island, Holei Sea Arch, a natural lava rock formation at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, has collapsed. Beloved Hawaii landmark Holei Sea Arch , a roughly 90-foot natural lava rock formation at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, has collapsed into the ocean after standing along Hawaii Island’s coast for centuries. The arch collapsed on Sunday following a rough stretch of storms that have hit the Big Island over the past several weeks. It was one of the destinations along Chain of Craters Road, the scenic drive that descends from the Kilauea summit area to the coast. At the end of the road, visitors could follow signs a short distance to a designated viewing area, where the massive arch extended from the cliffs over the ocean. A visitor from Massachusetts posted on Reddit about the disappearance after he expected to see the arch at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park on Sept. 28. After hearing that the arch had collapsed, a guide with Apau Hawaii Tours went to see it for himself on Sept. 30. In a YouTube video , he documented that the arch was gone and waves were breaking against the cliff. The Holei Sea Arch had been showing signs of instability for years. In 2022 , large surf from Tropical Storm Darby took a chunk of the natural sea arch and park rangers warned it could collapse at any time. items.article: Christa Pike made some horrific noises for nearly an hour during her botched execution ... and one local TV news anchor who was there is describing it for us ... and it sounds unpleasant. Tori Gessner -- an anchor for WKRN news in Tennessee -- joined us on "TMZ Live" Thursday to discuss what she saw and heard during Wednesday night's execution attempt ... which she says got off to a weird start when they didn't open the curtain for nearly an hour. Tori says it's normal for the curtain to be closed at first ... and that during this time, it's generally assumed IVs are being attached to the inmate. However, Tori says this usually takes 10 to 15 minutes ... but this time it took about an hour. During this time, she says she could hear some moaning, whimpering, and crying. Eventually, the curtains did open, and Tori says the gallery could see Christa lying on a gurney ... and she delivered what were supposed to be her last words. Tori says the pentobarbital was then administered ... and Christa entered the widely reported "snoring phase" -- before the curtain closed again for a few minutes. When they reopened, Tori says more pentobarbital was administered. However, the curtains closed again ... and the reporters could hear her "snore-squeak" for close to an hour before they were all sent home. She says it was "difficult to listen to."

items.text: Walking is great after 50, but it does not work every muscle: Physiotherapist suggests these 4 exercises for better strength
items.article: Walking is one of the easiest ways to stay active, but it does not train every part of the body in the same way. That is the point behind a recent exercise suggestion from fitness coach Will Harlow, who encourages people over 50 to pair their daily walks with a few simple strength moves. His routine takes only a few minutes and needs little or no equipment. A regular walk works the heart and keeps the legs moving, but strength training gives muscles a different kind of workload. This becomes particularly important with age, when maintaining muscle strength can support everyday movements and physical independence. Harlow's approach is deliberately simple. Instead of turning exercise into a long gym session, he suggests adding four movements across the day. Harlow recommends 10 push-ups, with wall push-ups or floor versions depending on ability. The movement mainly challenges the chest, shoulders and arms. There is no need to begin with a floor push-up if that feels too difficult. A wall or elevated surface can make the movement more manageable while still providing resistance. The sit-to-stand may look almost too ordinary to count as exercise. That is precisely what makes it useful. Harlow suggests 10 repetitions from a chair. The movement trains the legs and hips while closely resembling something done repeatedly in daily life, getting up from a chair. items.article: Mkutano House, at San Diego Zoo Safari Park, might just be the wildest dining experience in California. The thing to remember, if you’re dining at Mkutano House, is that the elephants are the most important guests. You might be sitting at your own assigned table, eating the food you ordered for yourself, but it’s their restaurant — even if they aren’t technically allowed inside. “It definitely comes with some different operating parameters,” Pat McTigue, executive director of the San Diego Zoo Safari Park , told SFGATE. Mkutano House is the new restaurant inside the Safari Park in Escondido , California, a much larger and more remote counterpart to the San Diego Zoo. It opened with the new Elephant Valley preserve, which houses the park’s nine African elephants. Eight years in the making, it’s the newest and arguably the most elaborate elephant sanctuary in all of California — and with the restaurant’s location in the middle of the preserve, it certainly offers one of the wildest dining experiences in the state. As you sip on your cocktail made with African spirits and dine on African-inspired cuisine, those elephants will nearly come right up to your table, with only a small but effective lagoon separating the enormous pachyderms from the diners. “The wildlife is at the heart of everything we do,” McTigue added. “... Chris Brown 's former housekeeper has agreed to accept a lower damages award in her dog bite case against the singer after a judge gave her a choice -- accept the reduced amount or take the risk of a new trial on damages. In court docs obtained by TMZ ... Maria Avila -- who claimed she was viciously attacked by Brown's dog in his Tarzana home in 2020 -- agreed to the new $9.5 million in damages. Avila initially won a $12.9 million judgment ... but a Los Angeles County Superior Court judge said not so fast. Because the judge felt there was insufficient evidence of nerve damage and other issues, they signed off on the singer's request for a new trial on damages unless Avila agreed to the lowered amount -- which, according to newly filed docs in the case, she just did. The new amount is broken down into the following proposed allocations -- $3.85 million for past non-economic losses, $5.4 million for future non-economic losses, and $250,000 for future medical expenses. items.article: The man who took the famous arrest image says the military is not doing enough to reassure locals. The man who took a now-famous photo of the five men arrested at RAF Fairford said he thought nothing of it until he woke up the following morning. "I saw the guys being arrested outside the house on Sunday morning and went back to bed and thought, 'oh, well they've got them now'," said the Whelford resident, who did not want to be named. "Then all hell broke loose at half past six in the morning." At a police information point at Fairford Community Centre earlier, he - along with other locals - said communication from the military base following the major security incident had been "poor". The US Air Force, which operates from RAF Fairford, has been approached for comment. A major investigation was launched after five men were arrested at RAF Fairford on Sunday on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. They have since been bailed. Earlier, Counter Terrorism Policing announced a 25-year-old man, a dual UK-Iranian national, had been arrested in London , on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts.

items.article: As the San Francisco Giants embark on an offseason filled with questions about the franchise, the biggest one to answer is who will replace Mike Krukow. As the San Francisco Giants embark on an offseason filled with questions about the franchise, arguably the biggest one to answer is who will replace broadcasting legend Mike Krukow . Krukow retired after 36 years as the team’s primary television analyst, with his last game fittingly happening last Sunday against the Dodgers, the team he grew up rooting for. Krukow has admitted he wanted to go out quietly but was convinced to announce his retirement all the way back on Aug. 6 , which is something Giants CEO Larry Baer is grateful for. “He put himself through a lot in the last five, six weeks,” Baer told SFGATE on Tuesday. “But announcing when he did and feeling the love, as it turned out, totally energized him. That was great. It turned out to be the right call.” The Giants were able to give Krukow a touching send-off and allow their fans to say goodbye. His longtime broadcasting partner and best friend Duane Kuiper brought both laughs and tears to Krukow with his actions on the day, with former teammates Bob Brenly and Will Clark giving touching speeches to their longtime friend. Krukow has admitted many times recently that he doesn’t want to retire, but his degenerative muscle disease has gotten to the point where he told NBC Sports Bay Area it is “becoming unsafe” to be anywhere but his Reno home on a regular basis. items.text: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
items.article: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective? A demonstrator in Massachusetts wearing a bridal gown takes part in a protest urging legislators to end child marriage. David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe/via Getty Images hide caption It's been a landmark year for activists seeking bans against child marriage in the U.S. On Sept. 30, California Governor Gavin Newsom signed Bill AB 1267 , setting 18 as the minimum age for marriage in the state, with no exceptions. The bill, sponsored by Unchained at Last and the California Commission on the Status of Women and Girls, was authored by Assemblymember Gail Pellerin. It repealed provisions that had allowed minors to marry with parental consent and judicial approval, a system that meant California had no statutory minimum marriage age. The law also removes the parallel exception that allowed minors to enter domestic partnerships. Its passage marks the culmination of a nearly decade-long campaign by survivors and advocacy groups to outlaw marriage before 18 in the state. California is now the 18th state to prohibit child marriage without exception; such marriages remain legal under varying restrictions in 32 other states. The signing also brought survivor voices to the forefront.
